chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I am eager for jihad and am active.' He said to him, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), 'So perform jihad in the way of Allah, for if you are killed, you will be alive with Allah, being provided for; and if you die, your reward has been established by Allah; and if you return, you will return from sins as you were born.'

He said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have two elderly parents who claim they are comforted by me and they dislike my going out.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'So stay content with your parents, and by the One in Whose hand is my soul, their being comforted by you for a day and a night is better than a year of jihad.'

key_terms.الْجِهَادِ: Striving or fighting in the way of God

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for serving elderly parents compared to jihad?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet (SAWW) establishes the hierarchy of virtues by prioritizing *birr al-walidayn* (righteousness to parents) over the collective obligation of jihad, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence. The narration highlights that the spiritual merit of alleviating parents' loneliness for a single day and night surpasses a year of military struggle, emphasizing that filial piety is a continuous, high-value worship. This context underscores the Shia scholarly view that serving parents is not merely a social duty but a supreme act of devotion that can substitute for other major ibadat under specific conditions.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to Rasool-Allahsaww and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! I am desirous regarding the Jihād actively’. So the Prophetsaww said: ‘So perform Jihād in the Way of Allahazwj, and if you are killed, you would happen to be alive in the Presence of Allahazwj being Sustained, and if you were to die (beforehand), so your Recompense would occur upon Allahazwj, and if you were to return, you would return from the sins just as you were born’.

He said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! For me there are parents who are aged, they claim that they are comforted by me and they dislike my going out’. So Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘So stay with your parents, for by the Oneazwj is Whose Hand is mysaww soul, their being comforted by you for one day and night is better than a Jihād for a year’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn Salim from Ahmad ibn al- Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Once a man came to the Messenger of Allah and said, ‘I am interested in Jihad (joining the army) O Messenger of Allah. I am active and light.’ The Imam said, ‘The Holy Prophet said, “Do Jihad (join the army) in the way of Allah, if you will be killed you will be living with Allah and will receive sustenance. If you die you will receive your reward from Allah, and if you return you will return free from sins as in the day you were born.”

The man then said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, my parents are old and they think my presence is a comfort for them and they do not like my going out.’ The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘Stay with your parents, I swear by the One in whose hand is my soul, that your parents’ receiving comfort from your presence with them for one day and night is more virtuous than Jihad for one year.’”
